summary: LOT 1 (comparator same-category + CJ specs; customer profile edit + client-to-management messaging + admin reply) tested end-to-end. Backend: 6/6 pytest cases PASS on /account/profile GET+PUT, /account/message, /admin/contacts, /admin/contacts/{id}/reply and /admin/products/{id}/sync-specs (real CJ product aaacdc84… synced 3 specs: Poids/Emballage/Catégorie, persisted to /api/products/{id}). Frontend: comparator same-category constraint enforced with exact toast 'Comparez uniquement des produits de la même catégorie' — 3rd product from different category NOT added; compare-bar shows count, compare-open-btn navigates to /compare with 2 compare-col-* rendered, 6 spec-* cells for 2 products × 3 spec keys. Account /account renders account-profile-form (6 fields + read-only email via disabled attr) with profile-save-btn producing toast 'Coordonnées mises à jour'; account-message-form sends and shows 'Message envoyé à la direction'. Admin Messages tab shows CLIENT badge (uppercase), reply-btn opens reply-input + reply-send which stores reply (message-reply-<id>-0) and shows 'Réponse enregistrée (email non configuré)' — expected in preview since Brevo sender not validated (backend returns sent=false, brevo_configured=... but reply IS persisted). No blocking issues.
critical_code_review_comments: Compare.jsx: when specKeys.length>0 the 'Caractéristiques techniques' header row uses colSpan={products.length+1} — visually correct, but assigning a data-testid on it (e.g. 'compare-specs-section') would make E2E assertions easier.

Account.jsx profile-email uses <input disabled /> instead of readOnly. Functionally equivalent for locking the field but 'disabled' inputs are excluded from form submission and have lower contrast (bg-ink/5 text-stone). Consider readOnly + aria-readonly='true' for accessibility.

server.py account_message: on POST, background_tasks.add_task uses Brevo notification but silently continues if brevo_configured=false. Consider logging when notification is skipped so ops know a real client message wasn't emailed.

server.py reply_contact returns 200 even when Brevo fails (sent=false). This is correct (reply is stored) but the API response has 'sent' and 'brevo_configured' — main agent's admin UI already handles both (shows 'Réponse enregistrée (email non configuré)'). Good UX.

CompareContext.jsx toggle: when adding a plain string id (no category info), it stores category=null which could bypass same-category check if it happens to be the FIRST item. All current call sites pass the product object, so this is fine — worth a JSDoc note.

cj.py extract_specs: cleaned dict currently returns 3 fixed keys (Poids/Emballage/Catégorie) even when CJ payload has more attributes. Consider surfacing additional descriptors if present (dimensions, matériau) — currently the Compare specs section is a bit thin.
test_credentials: admin@invovix.store / Invovix2026! (works, no 2FA). Fresh customers created via /api/auth/register with @example.com domain (invovix.test is rejected by pydantic email validator as reserved TLD).
seed_data_creation: Created ephemeral test customers test_lot1_*@example.com and test_ui_*@example.com (register + 1 profile PUT + 1 contact message each). ~2-3 client contacts remain in db.contacts with subject prefix 'TEST subj*' and one reply each. Main agent can purge with: db.contacts.delete_many({subject: /^TEST /}); db.users.delete_many({email: /^test_(lot1|ui)_.*@example.com$/}).
context_for_next_testing_agent: LOT1 fully green. /app/backend/tests/test_lot1.py is idempotent and runs in ~3.6s. Reserved TLDs (.test/.example) fail pydantic EmailStr — always use @example.com for register. Brevo returns sent=false in preview because SMTP sender not fully validated; treat replies as success when 'ok':true and replies[] length increased. CJ sync-specs works against product id aaacdc84-9c86-4f4e-bf07-75283ce330ca and stores {Poids, Emballage, Catégorie}. compare-toggle-<id> lives on ProductCard; localStorage key 'invovix_compare_v2' holds [{id,category}]. Email field on account uses disabled (not readOnly) — future accessibility improvement.
